maker: GELLO (P. Wu, Y. Shentu, Z. Yi, X. Lin, P. Abbeel)
name: GELLO (built for the target arm)

sources.title: P. Wu et al., GELLO: A General, Low-Cost, and Intuitive Teleoperation Framework for Robot Manipulators, arXiv:2309.13037 (HTML version)
sources.covers: the same kinematic structure as the target arm, the DYNAMIXEL XL330 servos and their encoder resolution, the robots built for, the bill of materials

note: GELLO is not one device: "Given a target robot arm, we build a GELLO controller device that has the same kinematic structure as the target arm, leveraging 3D-printed parts and economical off-the-shelf motors"; the paper built them for the UR5, the xArm7 and the Franka Panda ("The bill of materials for each GELLO device is less than $300"). Its joints map one to one to the follower's, so in DexVantage it leads with the follower's own model (leads "*", same_joints true). Its DoF is the target arm's (null here: 6 for the UR5, 7 for the Panda and xArm7). Servos "DYNAMIXEL XL330 series" with "high-resolution 12-bit encoders, enabling joint measurements within 0.088 of a mechanical degree" (joint_resolution_deg 0.088). Not stated in the paper: a sample rate, a latency, the mass, the power.

dof.quote: The target arm's: "GELLO is also effective for 7 DOF arms, such as the Panda and xArms".

workspace.quote: The workspace is the follower's own (joint to joint); the source states no separate volume.

joint_resolution_deg.quote: "these servos are equipped with high-resolution 12-bit encoders, enabling joint measurements within 0.088 of a mechanical degree"
